newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen climbing further at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen climbing further at open.

text.p: * Toronto stocks were expected to rise at the open after a strong post-Greenspan rally yesterday. * Analysts said traders will be watching for Greenspan comment at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.

Toronto stocks were expected to extend Tuesday's gains at the open on Wednesday but analysts said traders would keep an eye on the second leg of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to Congress.

MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie said North American stocks would be boosted again today by strong bonds and bills, which rallied on Tuesday after Greenspan delivered an upbeat report on the U.S. economy. But Beattie said Greenspan may be asked about Tuesday's market activity at a question and answer session beginning at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.

"I think we're going to open on a strong note but traders are going to be watching the 10 o'clock testimony pretty closely...he may be asked about yesterday's market activity and he could upset the market. It's hard to say, but there is that hurdle to still get through," Beattie said.
She said slipping gold prices may hurt the precious metals sub-index but the weakness would likely be offset by overall gains and climbing interest-sensitive issues.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index jumped more than one percent on Tuesday, adding 66.86 points to close at 6714.25.

In economic news this morning, the Canadian composite leading indicator rose 0.8 percent in June to 195.1 (base 1981) after a 0.7 percent rise in May. A Reuter survey of economists had forecast the index to rise 0.7 percent.
* Placer Dome Inc said overnight it turned a US$0.06 per share profit in the second quarter, compared to a loss of US$0.13 per share in the same period last year.
